llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions are consistent with a multi‑agent orchestration installer — it will modify OpenClaw agent config, create agent workspaces, and optionally install a background watcher; review scripts and consent before running.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (multi‑agent DAG dispatch, durable tracking, retries) matches what the files and SKILL.md actually do: copy agent templates, create per‑agent workspaces, write agent entries into openclaw.json, and set up task tracking. There are no unrelated credentials or external services required by default.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires the agent/operator to run the included setup scripts and to 'must first execute' an environment detection/installation step. The instructions explicitly tell the agent to derive SKILL_DIR, create symlinks, copy assets to ~/.openclaw/agents/<id>, write ~/.openclaw/configs/team-dispatch.json and modify/openclaw.json, and restart the Gateway. Those are high‑impact operations (write/modify system/user agent configuration and restart a service) — they are coherent with the skill's stated purpose but are intrusive and should be consented to and audited first. The skill also documents installing a low‑frequency watcher (background job) which implies persistent background behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no network install spec; everything is packaged as local scripts and assets. That reduces remote code fetch risk, but the included scripts will perform filesystem writes, create symlinks, and install/enable a watcher via system schedulers (openclaw-cron/launchd/systemd/cron). Installing scheduled/background jobs and rendering system scheduler units is a nontrivial installer action — review the scripts (watch-install, setup.sh, restart steps) before executing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The docs reference provider model names (openai-codex/gpt-5.2, etc.) and troubleshooting mentions OPENAI_API_KEY if the user enables an OpenAI provider, but that is optional and user‑supplied later. Notification integrations (Telegram) appear optional and disabled by default. Overall requested environment access is proportionate to the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The scripts will create persistent state under the user's home (~/.openclaw/skills, ~/.openclaw/agents, ~/.openclaw/configs, backups, tasks) and may install a background watcher (system scheduler). They will also modify openclaw.json and restart the Gateway to apply changes. While this persistence is needed for a durable dispatcher, it is intrusive and grants the skill long‑lived presence and the ability to affect agent behavior and background processing — inspect and back up existing openclaw.json/configs before running setup.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing/running setup.sh:
- This package is coherent with its purpose but is intrusive: it will write files under ~/.openclaw, copy agent templates into ~/.openclaw/agents, modify openclaw.json (agents.list and main.subagents.allowAgents), create task/workspace directories (default ~/work), and restart the OpenClaw Gateway.
- It may install a background watcher (cron/launchd/systemd) that periodically scans task state — decide if you want that running and inspect watch-install/watch-uninstall scripts first.
- Because these are filesystem and service changes, back up ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and any existing configs before running. Prefer running the scripts manually in a shell so you can read and approve each step instead of allowing full automatic execution by an agent.
- Review the scripts (scripts/setup.sh, watch-install.sh, setup-config.sh, verify.sh, uninstall.sh) for any network calls, remote downloads, or commands you don't recognize. From the provided files there are no obvious remote downloads, but the truncated files should be checked if you plan to run them.
- If you do not want automatic modifications, consider extracting only the templates you need and making the openclaw.json changes yourself, or run setup.sh in a safe environment (VM/container) first.
- If you want to enable notifications or model providers later, be aware you'll need to supply provider credentials (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY) and that the skill may configure model names in agent definitions — do so intentionally.
- If anything is unclear, request a diff of what setup.sh will change (or run it with a dry‑run flag if available) and confirm you understand the Gateway restart and background job installation behavior.
